headline: Highest risk is cascading error: marker can act on content while Awesome-Prompt-Engineering can supply untrusted prompt material, but direct data leakage and compliance issues are limited by marker's no-network/no-filesystem profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a prompt-writing resource, so it can supply attacker-controlled prompt text; marker is a runnable document processor, making it plausible that prompt-like content is ingested during document workflows. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven, but uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF marker ingests prompt text from documents or templates as instructions
IF the pair is connected by copy-paste or file-based handoff
mitigations: Treat all imported prompt text as untrusted input
Add a manual review step before marker processes prompt-heavy documents
Use separate workspaces for prompt libraries and document inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no I/O surfaces; B has no filesystem read/write and no network egress. With no shared workspace or outbound channel shown, leakage between them is not a plausible default pathway, though the documentation is sparse.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies sensitive document content from marker into Awesome-Prompt-Engineering workflows
IF a shared workspace is introduced outside the documented profiles
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not paste sensitive documents into prompt repositories
Verify marker remains offline before processing confidential files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is non-runnable and exposes no write or network capabilities. marker is runnable but explicitly lacks filesystem write, shell, subprocess, git, and network egress. There is no overlapping mutable surface, so a write conflict pathway is blocked.
conditions: IF marker is replaced with a version that can write files or modify git state
IF a separate orchestrator grants both agents shared mutable storage
mitigations: Avoid mounting a shared writable directory
Confirm no external orchestrator adds write permissions

D_cascading_error.rationale: marker is runnable and can process outputs from upstream sources, while Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a prompt-content repository that could feed unverified instructions or examples. The pair lacks documented verification or provenance controls, so downstream misuse is plausible in default document workflows.
conditions: IF marker consumes content derived from Awesome-Prompt-Engineering without a verification step
IF downstream automation treats marker output as authoritative
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before acting on marker output
Restrict automation to read-only review workflows

E_compliance.rationale: Neither profile shows regulated data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies. Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a content-writing resource and marker has no declared sensitive-data handling, so no compliance mismatch is evidenced here.
conditions: IF either agent is later used on regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII
IF a deployment adds retention or residency requirements not present in the profiles
mitigations: Document the data classes allowed for each agent
Keep regulated data out of this pair
Review residency and retention settings before deployment
